annotation.title_clean: Proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on harmonised rules on Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act) and amending certain Union Legislative Acts – IMCO/LIBE compromise amendments (Title III Chapter 4, Articles 16-29a, 40-51, Annexes V-VIII)
annotation.title_en: Proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on harmonised rules on Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act) and amending certain Union Legislative Acts – IMCO/LIBE compromise amendments (Title III Chapter 4, Articles 16-29a, 40-51, Annexes V-VIII)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament, Committee on the Internal Market and Consumer Protection (IMCO) and Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs (LIBE); Rapporteurs Benifei and Tudorache
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament IMCO-LIBE compromise amendments to the proposed EU AI Act, covering notified bodies, harmonised standards and common specifications, conformity assessment, CE marking, EU database registration, provider and deployer obligations, foundation models, confidentiality and AI literacy. Embodied content is limited to product-related high-risk AI, CE marking and Machinery Regulation interplay.
key_provisions_or_claims: Member States designate notifying authorities and notified bodies meeting independence, competence and cybersecurity requirements for third-party conformity assessment.
Conformity with harmonised standards or Commission common specifications gives a presumption of conformity for high-risk AI and foundation models.
Product-related high-risk AI follows the conformity assessment under existing New Legislative Framework law, including the Machinery Regulation; physical high-risk AI carries a physical CE marking.
Providers must run a quality management system, keep documentation for 10 years, register in an EU database and issue an EU declaration of conformity.
Deployers must carry out fundamental rights impact assessments; public authority deployers register their use in the EU database.
